question.prompt: Let \(\triangle A_0 B_0 C_0\) be a triangle whose angle measures are exactly \(59.999^\circ,\) \(60^\circ,\) and \(60.001^\circ.\) For each positive integer \(n\) define \(A_n\) to be the foot of the altitude from \(A_{n-1}\) to line \(B_{n-1}C_{n-1}.\) Likewise, define \(B_n\) to be the foot of the altitude from \(B_{n-1}\) to line \(A_{n-1}C_{n-1},\) and \(C_n\) to be the foot of the altitude from \(C_{n-1}\) to line \(A_{n-1}B_{n-1}.\) What is the least positive integer \(n\) for which \(\triangle A_n B_n C_n\) is obtuse?

solutions.title: Double the angle deviations
solutions.explanation:
To track the repeated altitude constructions, first find how one construction changes the angles. Measuring each angle's deviation from \(60^\circ\) will then make the iteration simple.

Consider an acute triangle \(ABC\), with \(\angle A=\alpha\). Let \(D,E,F\) be the altitude feet from \(A,B,C\), respectively. The right angles \(\angle ADB\) and \(\angle AEB\) place \(D\) and \(E\) on the circle with diameter \(AB\). Equal inscribed angles subtending chord \(AE\) give
\[
\angle ADE=\angle ABE=90^\circ-\alpha.
\]
Likewise, \(D\) and \(F\) lie on the circle with diameter \(AC\), so
\[
\angle ADF=\angle ACF=90^\circ-\alpha.
\]
Because the triangle is acute, \(E\) and \(F\) lie on the same side of \(BC\) as \(A\), and on opposite sides of \(AD\). Thus ray \(DA\) splits \(\angle EDF\), giving
\[
\angle EDF=180^\circ-2\alpha.
\]
The same reasoning applies at the other two feet. Therefore, whenever the input triangle is acute, its angles \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) become
\[
180^\circ-2\alpha,\qquad
180^\circ-2\beta,\qquad
180^\circ-2\gamma.
\]
In particular, an angle \(60^\circ+x\) becomes
\[
180^\circ-2(60^\circ+x)=60^\circ-2x.
\]
So a triangle with angle set
\[
60^\circ-d,\quad60^\circ,\quad60^\circ+d
\]
produces one with angle set
\[
60^\circ-2d,\quad60^\circ,\quad60^\circ+2d.
\]
Starting with \(d=0.001^\circ\), the deviation after \(n\) steps is therefore \(0.001^\circ\cdot2^n\), as long as each preceding triangle is acute.

Now
\[
2^{14}=16384,\qquad 2^{15}=32768.
\]
For every \(n\le14\), the largest angle predicted by this rule is at most
\[
60^\circ+16.384^\circ=76.384^\circ<90^\circ.
\]
Starting from the acute initial triangle, this verifies inductively that every triangle through index \(14\) is acute and that the rule remains applicable. Applying it once more gives the angles at index \(15\):
\[
27.232^\circ,\qquad60^\circ,\qquad92.768^\circ.
\]
This triangle is obtuse, so the least positive index is \(\boxed{15}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
